While Source [S1] does not explicitly define `MinkowskiBroadcastAddition`, the claim states that the subject class differs from it by performing element-wise multiplication instead of adding. - **Batch Indexing:** Ensure that `batch_indices` and `batch_rows` correctly map to the global features, which are typically reduced to the origin per batch [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that `batch_indices` and `batch_rows` are used to map global features (reduced to the origin) to the input coordinates. Source [S1] explicitly provides code within the `forward` method of `MinkowskiBroadcast`: `batch_indices, batch_rows = input.coordinate_manager.origin_map(input.coordinate_map_key)` followed by a loop `for b, rows in zip(batch_indices, batch_rows): broadcast_feat[rows] = input_glob.F[b]`. This confirms that these variables are indeed used to correctly map the global features to the corresponding rows in the batch. Source [S2] supports the general context of broadcasting reduced global features to input coordinates, though it does not detail the specific indexing mechanism. Since all factual assertions in the claim are present and supported by the evidence in Source [S1], the verdict is supported.
